_comment: REVIEWED CONTRACT for what a compiled rule must carry. ASTRA, PR #24 round 1:
a derivation cannot be the completeness authority. A variable-name heuristic
missed three real matcher reads, and an unrelated dict named `p` plus a module
with PATTERNS in a COMMENT each produced a false kill on a correct artefact.
Dictionary spelling is not evidence of access to a pattern dictionary.
So the authority is this file, and the gate FAILS CLOSED on any source key it
does not classify: a new pattern field cannot ship until someone puts it here
as consulted or as metadata. Derivation still runs and is reported as
DIAGNOSTIC evidence beside it, never as the verdict.
ROUND 2 WAS WRONG ABOUT THREE OF ITS FOUR METADATA KEYS, and gate (c) was
green for all three, because (c) grades the artefact against this file and
this file's metadata bucket was an assertion nobody had executed. Measured
2026-09-21 over the 136-case parity corpus, deleting each key from the
compiled rule set: `category` changed WHICH findings fire in 11 cases, and
`name` and `description` changed 43 finding records each. Only `mechanism`
was inert. controls/metadata_is_measured.mjs now re-measures the remaining
metadata keys on every run, so `metadata` is a measurement rather than a
claim. A reader that grades itself is what this whole file exists to stop.
WHAT THAT CONTROL DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH (ASTRA round 3, adopted): it
compares finding IDs, finding RECORDS and the decision over a 136-case
corpus. That is neither byte-identical whole-output comparison nor enough
cases to establish universal inertness, so the honest statement is: no
finding-ID, finding-record or decision difference was observed on these
cases. Point it at an older contract with `--contract <path>` to watch it
fail; a control that can only run green proves nothing about detection.
The derivation found none of this because it scopes the PYTHON matcher while
these read sites are in the JS Worker engine. That is a boundary of the
derivation AS IT EXISTS, not a proof that no static analysis could reach
them -- extending the analysis to the Worker source is possible.
`where` is the lowering. `record` means the compiler must emit the same key on
the compiled record with an equal value. `regex[].anchors` and `regex[].span`
are the measured lowering of the anchored lane: EVERY compiled regex entry of
an anchored rule carries the same anchor set and span (7 rules, 13 entries,
measured on v0.5.9). Regex SEMANTICS stay with the behavioural parity gates;
this file is about fields surviving compilation, not about what they match.

keywords.reason: measured on v0.5.9, 1554/1554 exact: the compiler emits the source's keywords minus SunglassesEngine.KEYWORD_DENYLIST, order preserved -- the same FP-guard strip the engine applies at index-build time (engine.py:468). The denylist is READ FROM THE TAGGED SOURCE, never listed here, so a change to it cannot silently pass this gate.

negation_immune.reason: measured on v0.5.9: 1548 rules omit it and the compiler emits false

regex.reason: the compiler transforms sources and adds guards/requires; entry COUNT is checked here and semantics are the parity gates' job

category.reason: reaches control flow twice, both measured 2026-09-21: engine.js:588/593 suppress a mechanism when a carrier of the SAME category already fired at >= severity, and policy.js:73-74 group findings by category for the corroboration rule. Deleting it leaves GLS-MECH-001 unsuppressed in 11 of 136 corpus cases. Filed as metadata in round 2 on no measurement.

name.reason: copied onto every finding at engine.js:423. It steers nothing -- 0 id and 0 decision deltas -- but deleting it changes 43 of the 136 corpus results, so a compiler that dropped it would rewrite the JSON a consumer reads while gate (c) stayed green.

description.reason: copied onto every finding at engine.js:426; same measurement as `name`, 43 changed records, 0 id and 0 decision deltas.

metadata._comment: Consulted by nothing AND emitted by nothing -- the compiler MAY drop these, and `mechanism` is dropped on the one rule that carries it. If it emits one it must EQUAL the source, and it may never invent one the source does not carry. This is no longer taken on anyone's word: controls/metadata_is_measured.mjs deletes every key listed here from the compiled rule set and requires the engine's finding IDs, finding records and decision to be unchanged over the parity corpus. That is a BOUNDED result, not universal inertness -- see the note in _comment. Adding a key here without that control going green is how round 2 shipped three wrong ones.
